en.title: Maximum Secondary Tasks When Each Day Has One Primary Task
en.description:
There are n primary tasks and n secondary tasks. Over n days, schedule exactly one primary task each day; each day may also take at most one secondary task, each task can be used only once, and a day's total duration must not exceed limit. Find the maximum number of secondary tasks. If some primary task alone exceeds the limit, return −1 according to this site's no-solution output convention. Zero durations are also judged by whether the total stays within the limit.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, editorial and tests; missing original bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the statement.
en.input: The first line contains n limit, the second line contains n primary values, and the third line contains n secondary values. The original statement gives no value bounds; on this site 1≤n≤100000, 0≤limit and all durations≤10^9. Inputs with a primary task over the limit are kept, and only the −1 no-solution encoding is added.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 2; 1; and -1, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Each primary task leaves a remaining capacity limit−primary; sort these in ascending order, and sort the secondary tasks in ascending order as well. Go through the capacities one by one: if the smallest unused secondary task fits, pair them; otherwise skip that capacity.
